title: Xylem Transport and Ascent of Sap: Cohesion–Tension and Hydraulic Limits
word_count_method: Saved HTML p.teaching-prose text only, stripped markup, whitespace-separated; excludes figures, tables, questions, references, navigation, and revision.

coverage_matrix.concept: Tracheids, vessel elements, pits, lignified walls
Sap composition and advective solute delivery
Cohesion–tension, adhesion, surface curvature and evaporation
Gravity, pressure budget, resistance and lumen-flow derivation
Root pressure, guttation and capillarity limits
Cavitation, embolism, air seeding and conditional recovery
Vulnerability curves, P50, safety margins, height limits
Potometer, pressure chamber, hydraulic conductivity and experimental controls
Integrated plant system and quantitative applications

scientific_review: Internal scientific pass checked source-aligned mechanisms and distinctions: force generation at leaf-wall interfaces, bulk flow and sap loading, hydrostatic and frictional losses, ideal cylindrical assumptions, root pressure limits, pit membrane air seeding, vulnerability and storage. Reviewed all 52 correct options; independently recomputed gravity, pressure, pore threshold, root head, capillary rise, conductivity loss, humidity potential and parallel conductance examples. Checked interpretation of potometry and pressure-chamber measurements, controls and artefacts. Synthetic datasets labeled.
editorial_review: Separate editorial/static pass reordered eighteen theory sections, inserted figures at relevant sections, retained established reader shell, corrected pressure-chamber gas inlet arrow and a question wording inconsistency, balanced answer letters while preserving all correct option text. Read saved HTML to verify teaching-word count, unique paragraphs and questions, all explanations, balanced markup, SVG titles/descriptions, anchors, ARIA references and zoom IDs; reader JS compiled.
deductions: Scientific: idealized models and context-dependent biological limits, no external review. Pedagogy: some dense quantitative sections. Illustrations: schematic/static inspection only. Assessment: original uncalibrated questions and some straightforward distractors. Reader: no actual mobile/browser or screen-reader interaction tested.
source_checks: Official revised January 2026 CSIR–UGC–DBT syllabus and separate Life Sciences syllabus, Unit 6.F; archived MP SET 2024 mirror; selected textbook, review and primary research records on xylem hydraulics, pressure measurement, air seeding, conductivity and height limits.
limitations: Internal self-assessment, not independent scientific peer review.
MP SET source is a 2024 archived mirror, not a current official MPPSC-hosted copy.
Interactive reader, actual mobile rendering and screen-reader tests not performed.
Not all full-text reference articles or every reference URL independently tested.
